final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a policy-bounded interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally correct: the evidence supports only a controlled, reversible rollout context and does not support any claim that rollout controls cure the weakness. But the decisive compliance predicate remains unresolved. Admissible evidence shows the exposed segment remains in scope, policy requires disclosure unless there is approved risk acceptance, and the only risk-acceptance document is an incomplete draft. The record still lacks the final launch artifact showing the required disclosure was actually made. That means a present-tense claim that the model can be certified for launch now is still not supported on the available evidence. This is not upgraded to compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is not merely descriptive; it is an unmet policy condition.
remaining_concerns: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy requires the material limitation to be disclosed before launch unless it is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not mention the exposed segment.
The record still does not include the final model card or launch artifact proving the required disclosure was completed.
Rollout controls, rollback, monitoring, and a 7% initial rollout are mitigating context only and do not satisfy the disclosure predicate while exposure remains.
